subject: Escape hatch & feature transplantation for Clearline upgrade
messages:
From: Elena Torres <e.torres@clearlinehealth.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood-inference.com
Cc: Chris Huang <chris.huang@clearlinehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Upgrade ask — moving features, rollback and proration questions

Diego,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team is aligned that we need higher throughput for our triage pipeline and we'd like to explore upgrading from Compact -> Throughput for the pilot. A couple of things we need clarity on before we move forward:

- Can we transplant specific features from our current package into the higher tier rather than adopting the default bundle? For example we rely heavily on prefix/KV caching and the on-demand cold-start guard; we don't need multi-region replication yet.
- If we commit to a 90-day pilot at the higher tier and it doesn't hit our latency/cost targets, what's the escape hatch (rollback) look like? Proration? Credits?
- Any constraints on rolling back model variants (quantized versus full FP) that we should be aware of — we want to preserve output parity during the trial.

I've attached a feature map (Clearline_feature_map.xlsx) that shows what we'd like to carry forward. Can you outline a proposal with pricing and the rollback guardrails?

Elena
Elena Torres
Head of ML Platforms | Clearline Health
--
Attachment: Clearline_feature_map.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood-inference.com>
To: Elena Torres <e.torres@clearlinehealth.com>
Cc: Chris Huang <chris.huang@clearlinehealth.com>, ben.carter@redwood-inference.com, lauren.bishop@redwood-inference.com
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Upgrade ask — moving features, rollback and proration questions

Elena — great to hear the pilot looks like a good fit. High level answers first; I'll follow up with an internal note to get concessions validated and share a formal proposal by EOD Tuesday.

1) Feature transplantation: Yes — we can do a tailored composition for the pilot. We support pick-and-choose feature gates (prefix/KV caching, cold-start guard, specialized batching config) and will exclude multi-region replication. Operationally we'll map each selected feature to a flag in the tenant config so it can be toggled without a full migration.

2) Escape hatch: Recommend a 30-day rollback window during which we offer:
  - Prorated refund of the incremental tier delta for unused days OR a one-time credit equal to one month of the incremental committed throughput (your choice).
  - Automated rollback script that restores previous tenant flags and reserved capacity. We will perform a dry-run snapshot before switching to avoid drift.

3) Model/quantization constraints: We'll pin the serving variant used in the pilot. Rolling back will restore the previous variant and KV state where possible; note that some quantized-only optimizations (if enabled) will require a warm KV rebuild on rollback — typically 1–4 hours of warm-up depending on cache size. We'll document expected latency delta during warm-up.

Next steps: Ben and Lauren — can you confirm approval band for: (a) 90-day pilot with 15% first-90-days discount on the incremental tier fee, or (b) 10% discount + one-month incremental credit? I want to keep the customer choice. Also confirm whether legal needs an amended SOW for feature-level composition.

Elena, I'll attach a short proposal once I have approvals.

Best,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Exec | Redwood Inference
--

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood-inference.com>, lauren.bishop@redwood-inference.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Upgrade ask — moving features, rollback and proration questions

Diego / Lauren — quick internal note:

- Margin check: A 15% concession for the first 90 days is heavier than our standard pilot scale. I support the customer choice model, but prefer option (b): 10% + one-month incremental credit. That preserves revenue and gives the customer a clear escape economics.
- Escape credit mechanics: One-month incremental credit should be applied to the first invoice after downgrade automatically (no manual adjustments). That avoids finance churn.
- Legal/SOW: Small SOW amendment for feature composition is fine — it should call out the toggleable feature flags and the rollback dry-run clause. No need for a full contract redline.

If Diego wants to offer 15% instead (to close faster) get me a note with expected ARR impact and I'll escalate to pricing.

Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Mid-Market Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood-inference.com>
To: Elena Torres <e.torres@clearlinehealth.com>
Cc: Chris Huang <chris.huang@clearlinehealth.com>, ben.carter@redwood-inference.com, lauren.bishop@redwood-inference.com, karthik.iyer@redwood-inference.com
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Upgrade ask — moving features, rollback and proration questions

Elena — thanks for the feature map. Based on internal feedback here's a concise proposal (attached as proposal_v1.pdf) and next steps summary: 

Proposal summary:
- Pilot: 90 days on Throughput tier composed with only the features you requested (prefix/KV caching, cold-start guard, weighted batching). Multi-region replication excluded.
- Pricing: option A (preferred by Redwood): 10% discount on the incremental tier fee for the pilot period + one-month incremental throughput credit applied if you exercise the rollback.
           option B (accelerator): 15% discount for the first 90 days (no extra credit).
- Escape hatch: 30-day window after pilot start during which you may revert. Reversion options: prorated refund of incremental days OR apply the one-month credit to your next invoice (your choice). Automated rollback will restore feature flags; note 1–4 hour warm-up for KV rebuilds.
- SOW & sign: small amendment documenting feature flags and rollback dry-run; no full contract redline expected. DocuSign link in the attached proposal.

Requested next steps from you:
1) Pick option A or B and confirm which rollback payout you prefer (prorated refund vs one-month credit).
2) If option A, we'll issue proposal_v1.pdf and DocuSign. If option B, I'll request the accelerated concession approval but we should be able to proceed the same day.
3) Schedule a 30-minute runbook call with our infra team (suggest Thu 24 Sep 10:00 PT) to agree on the dry-run steps and KV snapshot cadence.

Happy to jump on a quick call this afternoon to walk through the proposal.

Thanks — looking forward to getting Clearline on the Throughput pilot.

Diego
Senior Account Exec | Redwood Inference
--
Attachment: proposal_v1.pdf (proposal stub, includes DocuSign link)
